page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E2.8 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7551 processor. Utilizing the x86_64 architecture, this instance provides 8 physical CPU cores configured with two threads per core, yielding 16 dedicated virtual CPUs operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz. System memory totals 64.0 GB of RAM, preserving a standard 1:4 ratio of vCPUs to memory (4.0 GB per vCPU).

This server instance contains no onboard local storage, necessitating external network-attached block volumes for persistent data needs. Similarly, the shape lacks hardware accelerators, containing zero GPUs. Network provisioning includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Because the instance relies on first-generation AMD EPYC architecture at a 2.0 GHz clock speed, it trades peak single-core throughput for cost-efficient multi-threaded compute density across its 16 dedicated vCPUs.

Given its balanced ratio of compute to memory, VM.Standard.E2.8 is appropriate for horizontal enterprise workloads, mid-tier web serving, continuous integration and build nodes, background batch processing, and non-specialized application hosting where extreme single-thread speed or specialized GPU acceleration is not required.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E2.8 is a general-purpose instance configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs and 64.0 GB of RAM, derived from 8 physical cores on an AMD EPYC 7551 processor running at 2.0 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local storage or GPU accelerators, relying on remote block storage for operational disk needs. Network configuration includes a single complimentary public IPv4 address. With dedicated core allocation and moderate clock rates, this shape provides a cost-effective platform for multi-threaded enterprise application hosting, middle-tier services, build pipelines, and standard web servers.
